Final visualization

Your final, explanatory visualization goes below. Include a short write-up: what does it communicate, why is this the best way to communicate it, and how robust is the finding?

## ---- Top left: national averages -------------------------------------------

## National shares over all pupils of all regular primary schools (not only
## our analysis sample): HAVO+ advice and test results at target level
national_havo <- advice_clean |>
  summarise(share = sum(HAVO + HAVO_VWO + VWO) / sum(n_groep8)) |>
  pull(share)
national_target <- levels_clean |>
  summarise(
    share = sum(
      pct_maths_1s * n_maths + pct_reading_2f * n_reading +
        pct_writing_2f * n_writing,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ) / sum(n_maths + n_reading + n_writing)
  ) |>
  pull(share)

national <- tibble(
  measure = c(
    "Test results at\ntarget level",
    "Pupils with\nHAVO+ advice"
  ),
  share = c(national_target, national_havo)
) |>
  # first row on top
  mutate(measure = factor(measure, levels = rev(measure)))

## Bar chart: each bar on a grey 100% track, value printed next to it
p_national <- ggplot(national, aes(y = measure)) +
  geom_col(aes(x = 1), fill = "grey90", width = 0.6) +
  geom_col(aes(x = share), fill = "#1B3A5C", width = 0.6) +
  geom_text(
    aes(x = share, label = scales::percent(share, accuracy = 1)),
    hjust = 1.15, colour = "white", fontface = "bold", size = 7
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, 1), expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "The Netherlands on average",
    subtitle = "All pupils of regular primary schools, 2024-2025",
    x = NULL, y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 16) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 14, colour = "black")
  )

## ---- Top right: 100 pupils per group ---------------------------------------

## HAVO+ share each group's regression line predicts for a school whose test
## results equal the national average
group_havo <- group_fit(
  schools, "pct_havo_plus",
  at = national_target, groups = levels(schools$disadvantage)
)
group_people <- tibble(
  disadvantage = factor(names(group_havo), levels = names(group_havo)),
  havo = group_havo,
  n_havo = round(100 * group_havo)
)

## Outline of one pupil icon (head + shoulders) centred on (0, 0) in a
## 1 x 1 cell
circle <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 30)
shoulders <- seq(0, pi, length.out = 20)
pupil_head <- tibble(
  x = 0.15 * cos(circle), y = 0.24 + 0.15 * sin(circle), part = "head"
)
pupil_body <- tibble(
  x = c(0.3 * cos(shoulders), -0.3, 0.3),
  y = c(-0.12 + 0.28 * sin(shoulders), -0.42, -0.42),
  part = "body"
)
pupil_shape <- bind_rows(pupil_head, pupil_body)

## 100 pupils per group on a 10 x 10 grid (filled row by row from the top
## left); the first n_havo of them get HAVO+ advice
people <- group_people |>
  cross_join(tibble(pupil = 1:100)) |>
  mutate(
    col = (pupil - 1) %% 10,
    row = 9 - (pupil - 1) %/% 10,
    status = if_else(pupil <= n_havo, as.character(disadvantage), "other")
  ) |>
  cross_join(pupil_shape) |>
  mutate(x = col + x, y = row + y, id = paste(pupil, part))

## Percentage printed under each grid
people_labels <- group_people |>
  mutate(label = paste0(n_havo, " of 100 pupils\nget HAVO+ advice"))

p_people <- ggplot(people, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  geom_polygon(aes(group = id, fill = status)) +
  geom_text(
    data = people_labels, aes(x = 4.5, y = -1.6, label = label),
    size = 5.5, lineheight = 0.9, fontface = "bold",
    colour = disadv_colours[as.character(people_labels$disadvantage)]
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~disadvantage) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(disadv_colours, other = "grey85")) +
  coord_fixed(ylim = c(-2.4, 9.5), clip = "off") +
  labs(
    title = paste0(
      "100 pupils at a school where ",
      scales::percent(national_target, accuracy = 1),
      " of test results reach the target level"
    ),
    subtitle = paste(
      "Same test results as the national average, but how many get",
      "HAVO+ advice\ndepends on how disadvantaged the school is"
    )
  ) +
  theme_void(base_size = 16) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(margin = margin(t = 4, b = 10)),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 15, margin = margin(b = 6)),
    panel.spacing = unit(1.5, "lines")
  )

## ---- Bottom: HAVO+ advice by test results ----------------------------------

## Scatterplot from Part 1, with the gap between the least and the most
## disadvantaged schools marked at 60% of results at target level
gap_havo <- group_fit(schools, "pct_havo_plus", at = 0.6)
p_havo <- make_scatter(
  schools, "pct_havo_plus",
  title = "Pupils with HAVO or higher advice by school test results",
  y_label = "Share of pupils with HAVO+ advice", show_legend = TRUE
) |>
  add_gap_label(gap_havo, at = 0.6, label_x = 0.98, label_y = 0.1, hjust = 1)

## ---- Combine ---------------------------------------------------------------

top_row <- plot_grid(
  p_national, p_people,
  nrow = 1, rel_widths = c(1, 2)
)
plot_grid(
  top_row, p_havo,
  ncol = 1, rel_heights = c(1, 1.15)
)
